reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all 7 files and found them safe. The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR practices for -bin packages: downloading prebuilt binaries from official GitHub releases with pinned SHA256 checksums, no obfuscated code, no suspicious network requests, and standard packaging operations (extract, install, create wrappers). The qwen model's inconclusive result was due to API errors (HTTP 400) when auditing .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml, not security findings. The openrouter/free report is advisory and crashed on initial PKGBUILD parsing. All successfully reviewed files are standard metadata/configuration with no executable content.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from tool failures, not security findings. qwen encountered HTTP 400 errors when auditing .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml, resulting in inconclusive status for those files. deepseek successfully reviewed all files including these two and found them safe (standard gitignore and nvchecker config). The openrouter/free report crashed with a JSONDecodeError and is marked advisory. There is no actual disagreement about security - only about whether tool errors should prevent a verdict.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .gitignore and .nvchecker.toml due to HTTP 400 API errors
openrouter/free model crashed on initial PKGBUILD audit with JSONDecodeError and did not proceed to other files
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, JSON parse errors) should not result in inconclusive verdicts when the files in question are low-risk metadata files that other models have successfully audited
The audit tool should distinguish between 'could not audit due to tool error' and 'found potential security issues' - these require different handling
When one model successfully audits all files and finds them safe, and another model's gaps are due to tool errors on non-executable files, the safe verdict should prevail
Advisory reports with tool errors should be clearly marked as providing no verdict signal, not just context
